title: perf(server): background PR discovery no longer delays git status after a restart
author: juliusmarminge
head: 04e36555e5296a406edafa29ef720b2466827a5f
body:
After a server restart, git status stalls for one to two minutes. On cups (nightly 4247) the startup PR backfill and the settlement sweep ran 100–200 PR lookups per minute at each of the three boots in the last 24h (11-05 16:33, 17:42, 11-06 03:00). Each lookup runs about 15 git commands, and every git command in the process shares one 8-slot pool (`gitProcesses` in `GitVcsDriverCore.ts`). So user-facing `localStatus` waited behind discovery: all 14 of cups' `localStatus` calls over 3 s that day fell inside those three boot minutes. Fleet-wide on personal hosts, `lookupBranchPullRequest` went from 1.1 to 14.8/h with p95 17 s, and `localStatus` p99 reached 17 s.

In trace `7fc5e544f62d2e266dd03c3a6a004e64` (an 8.7 s lookup), each `GitVcsDriver.readConfigValue` span lasts 450–900 ms while its `runGitCommand` child takes 50–75 ms at the end. The rest of the time is spent waiting for a pool slot.

**Fix:** a `GitVcsDriver.BackgroundGitWork` context reference. When it is set, `execute` takes a slot from a separate 2-slot pool instead of the shared 8. `ThreadPullRequestServiceV2`'s refresh worker and `ThreadSettlementServiceV2`'s sweep set it, so discovery still runs but can never take the slots git status needs. Commands with long or no timeouts still bypass both pools, as before.

**Trade-off:** the startup backfill now spreads over a longer stretch, about 2 git processes at a time instead of up to 8. It is background work that nobody waits on.

title: fix(muse): recover from unavailable session views
author: Sidreyas
head: e9a00e1b9a7b73d16dfae052cc8fbd4c09ab3d76
body:
## Problem

Fixes #17804.

Muse can resume a session with `history.noneReason: "projectionUnavailable"` while still accepting `turn/start`. T3 ignored that reason and started work whose events could never arrive, leaving the thread running indefinitely.

## Change

Decode the existing history reason and reject that unavailable session before starting a turn. The existing orchestration recovery path then opens a fresh native session with the conversation handoff. Intentionally excluded history and empty cursors remain accepted.

## Scope and approval

This is a focused fix for an explicit provider protocol failure. It uses the existing session recovery mechanism, adds no settings or model instructions, and changes no client UI or T3 wire contracts. Web, desktop, and mobile receive the same server state; other provider adapters are unchanged. Submitted under the small, obvious bug-fix exception.

## Verification

Windows, Node.js 26.12.1, checkout-local locked Effect 4.1.2, Vite+ 1.4.0, Muse SDK 1.4.6.

- Baseline, from `packages/provider-muse`: `vp test run --config ../../vite.config.ts --dir . src/server/adapter.test.ts -t 'closes a newly opened host'`: 1 failed / 1 passed. The unavailable-projection row failed with `expected 'Success' to equal 'Failure'`.
- Fixed: `vp test run --config ../../vite.config.ts --dir . src/server/adapter.test.ts src/server/protocol.test.ts`: 43 tests passed. Covers host cleanup, rejection before any turn request, and normal resume with excluded h [...]

title: fix(clients): dictating a citation comment or preview annotation uses the full width
author: juliusmarminge
head: 957b7b982307825117b4c39cb33304b27f6b7ee7
body:
## Problem

While you dictate, the recording controls sit in a fixed-width (256px) pill. In the citation comment box, that pill wraps above Cancel/Save but doesn't fill the row. In the browser preview's annotation popover, it adds a second row under the text field, next to an Attach button you can't use until dictation ends. Its Cancel/Finish buttons also render square inside the round pill.

## Change

- **Citation comment:** while dictation is active, the controls get their own row and the pill fills it. The pill now carries `data-slot="voice-input-pill"`, and the editor stretches it from outside, so the composer, Settings, PR and diff forms that share the pill are unchanged.
- **Preview annotation:** while dictation is active, the recording controls take the text field's place in the one-line composer row, and Attach is hidden. The controls drop the pill border and background to match the chat composer's. The textarea stays in the DOM, visually hidden with `sr-only`, and takes focus once when dictation starts, so Enter still finishes and attaches. When dictation ends, it comes back and is measured again so a long transcript gets its real height. The pill is only moved when its parent changes, so level updates don't blur a focused button. Errors still show on their own row.
- The Cancel/Finish/Skip buttons are round: `createButton`'s `rounded-md` sorted after `rounded-full` in the generated CSS and won. `AnnotationStyles.generated.ts` is regenerated.

## Scope and approval
 [...]

title: fix(web): the citation comment box opens at the quote instead of sliding in from the corner
author: juliusmarminge
head: 0fc0c457067238ce4f59965cca4e265cd4b1dca6
body:
## Problem

The citation comment box slides in from the top-left corner of the window every time it opens, instead of appearing at the quoted text.

## Change

https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/30623 gave this popover `keepMounted`, so dictation's setup dialog can replace it without losing the draft. A small, focused fix for a visible regression from https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/30623, reported by a maintainer (Julius). It touches only the popover positioner's transition class plus one test case.

## Verification

- A new case in `AssistantCitationChip.browser.test.tsx` asserts that no transform/top/left transition is running once the popover is positioned. It fails on `main` and passes here.

title: ci(release): macOS arm64 stops compressing a pnpm store it cannot save
author: t3dotgg
head: 4835a91a04f0749c306c98d9385524ffceac9c75
body:
Both release Mac jobs install the same filtered workspace on the same ARM64 runner type, so they save the pnpm store under one cache key. On a cold store both compress it, and one then fails with "Unable to reserve cache". The arm64 job pays this on the release critical path.

Now the release's macOS arm64 job passes `save_pnpm_store: false`, and macOS x64 saves the store alone. Both jobs still restore and install. Staged-install and native caches stay per target. Other callers, such as the lone arm64 preview, keep the default and still save. The stacked-PR save rule from #31937 is unchanged.

**Measured** (65 release runs from Oct 28 to Nov 6, read-only job metadata and logs):
- 30 runs saved a new Mac pnpm store, so both Macs compressed it. 23 were new lockfile keys, and 7 re-saved a key after eviction. #31937 can reduce only the second group.
- In 12 sampled logs, each Mac spent 19-21s compressing on a full miss and 9-11s after a fallback hit. The losing job's work was discarded each time.
- macOS arm64 finished after macOS x64 in 65 of 65 runs. It was the last of the five desktop jobs in 56.

**Modeled, not measured:** skipping that compression should cut about 10-20s from the arm64 job on cold runs. That is usually the release's last desktop job. No release ran for this PR.

**If x64 fails before its save** (about 1 minute in, right after install), no store is saved, and the next release starts cold once. That is the same cost as one eviction today.

title: perf(release): fetch the nightly Android APK in a background step
author: t3dotgg
head: 47cc5e5d2d01a5bdb3d28735ef0f5b536d1a3a8d
body:
## Problem

Nightly releases attach Play's internal Android APK (about 280 MB). The publish job fetched it in its own step, after the artifact downloads, so the release waited for it. In the last 12 published nightlies that step took 21–23 s four times and 4–6 s eight times (mean 10.75 s, median 5.5 s). [21-second run](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/42137832094/job/127634017341) · [4-second run](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/42182419098/job/127777136475)

## Change

The fetch is now a native GitHub Actions background step (`background: true`) in the existing publish job. On a nightly, it starts after checkout and dependency setup succeed. It has `continue-on-error: true` and `timeout-minutes: 5`. It writes to `$RUNNER_TEMP/android-apk`. The runner empties that directory at the start of each job.

`wait: android_apk` comes right after the CLI checksums. This is before the manifest merge scripts load workspace packages and before release notes start. Only the fetch process gets the Play key, and it has stopped before any repo script runs. `exec` makes node the step's own process, so the runner's stop signals reach node.

The asset list adds the staged APK only when `steps.android_apk.outcome` is `success`. The current mirror writes a temporary file and renames it on success. If a failed or timed-out fetch leaves a partial APK in staging, the outcome check excludes it. A skipped step has no outcome, so stable, preview and no-change runs list  [...]

title: perf(release): macOS CLI notarization no longer blocks the desktop build
author: t3dotgg
head: 2e6a7c0a2f6563a1ccd16273feb20e5aace7a287
body:
## Problem

On arm64 macOS the release job sat idle while Apple notarized the standalone CLI, and only then started building the desktop app, which goes through its own notarization. Nothing in the desktop build needs the CLI's approval.

## Change

On sources with deferred notarization, the CLI submits first. The desktop builds while Apple reviews the CLI. The Mac job uploads the CLI archive only after Apple returns `Accepted`.

- `scripts/build-cli-archive.ts --notary-submission-file ` submits without `--wait` and records the submission id. A new `await-notarization --submission-file ` subcommand runs `notarytool wait` and fails unless the status is `Accepted`. It also fails when notarization is configured but no submission was recorded, when a submission exists without credentials, and when notarytool fails. Rejected submissions print `notarytool log`.
- The archive bytes do not change: a bare executable cannot be stapled, so the ticket lives with Apple either way. CLI signing, desktop signing and stapling are unchanged.
- `release-desktop.yml`: the macOS CLI upload moves after "Build desktop artifact" and a new "Await CLI notarization" step. It keeps `compression-level: 0` from [#31942](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/31942). If Apple does not accept, the job fails before uploading the CLI or the desktop, so the release job (which requires `desktop_mac_arm64` success) never runs. Both CLI steps create the key file with mode 0600 in a private temporary directory.  [...]

title: perf(ci): release uploads stop recompressing installers and CLI archives
author: t3dotgg
head: 3d6f30bf96ac337ded84fe30f370f4f937b96e71
body:
Release builds upload installers and CLI archives that are already compressed, but `upload-artifact` deflates them again at level 6 by default. That costs CPU and saves almost nothing.

The `Upload CLI archive` and `Upload build artifacts` steps now set `compression-level: 0`, so the files are stored in the artifact zip as-is. Nothing else changes: same names, paths and files, and the verify-input upload keeps level 1.

### What is in these artifacts

Every large file is already compressed: `.dmg` (zlib UDIF), `.zip` (deflate), `.blockmap` (gzip), `.tar.gz`, `.deb` (xz), `.AppImage` (zstd squashfs) and the NSIS `.exe`. The only other files are two small `.yml` files.

### Measured

I downloaded the 11 desktop and CLI artifacts from [release run 42137832094](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/42137832094) (read-only), then rebuilt each artifact zip locally with zlib in two ways: stored, and deflate level 6. I unzipped both and compared each restored file's size and SHA-256 to the original. All files matched.

title: ci: stacked PRs stop evicting the shared pnpm cache
author: t3dotgg
head: c486f0b1dacbf5a64853eab29d3e04b69d70d836
body:
Stacked PRs were evicting the shared CI cache. A PR whose base is not `main` saves a ~1 GB pnpm store that only its own reruns can read.

Measured from Blacksmith logs and cache inventory:

- 145 full Linux x64 pnpm stores were saved between two Mac releases. 126 of them came from stacked PRs, 16 from default-base PRs, and 3 from `main` pushes.
- 19 stacked PRs held 17.71 GiB of the 24.55 GiB inventory. Those entries used only 2 distinct keys, so most were duplicate copies.
- Example: [this Linux job](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/42179170254/job/127764516212) on a stacked PR restored a fallback store, downloaded 1 package, and then uploaded a 1,001,159,631-byte copy.

Fix: `Save pnpm store` now runs only when the event is not `pull_request`, or the PR base is the repo's default branch. Stacked PRs still restore and install as before. title: ci(release): npm publish no longer checks out and installs the workspace
author: t3dotgg
head: 99278b342f8e3c859561edb6a322ecfb093b7bc5
body:
## Problem

`publish_cli` checks out the workspace and installs dependencies just to build and publish a ~3.6 KB `t3.tgz`. On [the example run](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/actions/runs/42137832094/job/127634717026) checkout took 12s and setup 34s, while building took under 1s and publishing 5s.

## Change

Now `build_bundle`, which already has the workspace installed, builds the version-matched launcher after the JS bundle upload and hands the tarball off as an `npm-launcher` artifact. The JS build step and its prerequisites are unchanged.

`publish_cli` stays on the GitHub-hosted runner, gated on a successful GitHub Release, with OIDC and `--provenance`. It now:
- checks out only `setup-ci-deps`, `package.json` and `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
- sets up the project's Node.js through `setup-ci-deps` with `install: "false"`
- fails unless `build_bundle` output a valid artifact ID for its own `npm-launcher` upload
- downloads only that artifact ID and checks the package version. The downloader compares SHA-256 when the artifact service supplies a digest and fails on a mismatch.
- runs `npm publish --access public --tag  --provenance ./npm-packages/t3.tgz`

**Why by ID.** download-artifact's name lookup takes the newest artifact with that name in the run. title: fix(azure-devops): existing pull requests are found for branches containing #
author: aotradovec
head: 3180dd3fb5c59574278c55c2584476cf893b4a2c
body:
## Problem

On Azure DevOps, a thread whose branch name contains `#` (for example `user/feat/12-(#34)-slug`) shows **Create PR** even though an active pull request for that branch already exists. The branch lookup finds nothing, so T3 offers to create a PR, and `az repos pr create` then fails because the PR exists.

Cause: the Azure CLI puts query values into the request URL unescaped (msrest's `format_parameters` documents that it assumes values are already quoted). A `#` starts a URL fragment, so the request is cut off there and Azure returns `200 []`, which T3 reads as "no PR".

The same applies to the other place T3 sends a user-controlled value through the query string: reading a changed file by path. A path containing `#` or `&` is truncated.

## Change

One root cause, two call sites. Both now pass the value through `encodeURIComponent`, which `az` forwards unchanged and Azure decodes:

- `AzureDevOpsCli.listPullRequests`: the source branch of `az repos pr list --source-branch`.
- `AzureDevOpsPullRequestCli.readItemContent`: the `path` query parameter of `az devops invoke`.

`createPullRequest` is untouched: it sends the branch in a JSON body, where encoding would create a branch literally named with `%23`. The other `az` arguments are numeric IDs, commit SHAs, or identities the extension resolves itself.

## Scope and approval

Very small, focused fix of an obvious bug (one argument in each of two calls, plus a test for each), so I am submitting it without a prior iss [...]

title: fix(web): tagging a thread by drag no longer scrolls the sidebar
author: t3dotgg
head: eed671fcca84690982ff714c15f92bc5380219df
body:
Dragging a thread from the sidebar into the composer to tag it scrolled the sidebar, often all the way to the bottom.

The path out of the list usually crosses dnd-kit's autoscroll edge zone at the bottom of the sidebar. At that point the drag is still a reorder drag, so dnd-kit autoscrolls fast. Autoscroll turns off once the pointer leaves the list, but the scroll has already happened.

The sidebar now saves its scroll position when a drag starts. It restores that position when the drag leaves the list to become a tag drag, and again on drop. Reordering inside the list still autoscrolls as before.

This works with #27691, which tunes reorder autoscroll (smaller edge zone, slower). That makes tag-drag scroll rarer, but leaving through the edge zone still scrolls. This PR removes the leftover scroll for tag drags. The two PRs change different lines.

title: fix(build): skip Koffi source builds during cross-packaging
author: Yash-Singh1
head: a65ae9735f0e25c8fda48c1e830a0ff6dc159e3d
body:
The macOS x64 release job fails while staging production dependencies on an ARM64 runner. Koffi's install script probes the running Node architecture, but the stage installs only x64 optional binaries. The missing ARM64 prebuild triggers a source build that fails with unresolved N-API/libuv symbols.

Disable Koffi lifecycle builds in the workspace approval policy. Koffi ships its native binaries in optional platform packages and loads them directly, so installation does not need a source build. Desktop and CLI staging already inherit this policy.

The dependency and build approval were introduced by #30625, authored and merged by Julius Marminge, with UtkarshUsername credited as co-author. The failed job installed Koffi 3.3.7 while the workspace lockfile used 3.3.6; the underlying issue is the host-architecture probe during cross-packaging.

Validation:
- Reproduced the same ARM64 linker failure locally with Koffi 3.3.7 and an x64-only staged install.
- Repeated a clean install with lifecycle builds disabled; installation succeeded.
- Loaded the staged x64 Koffi 3.3.7 binary using x64 Node 26.12.1 under Rosetta and called libc getpid(), which matched process.pid.
- `vp run check:changed` passed, including formatting, unused-patch validation, and affected typechecks.
- A full signed release build was not run locally.

title: perf(server): batch shutdown recovery commits
author: Yash-Singh1
head: 9be12daf445dc9e7a5a86e9f2265c0ffdad3ac25
body:
## Problem

Shutdown recovery committed each orphaned provider thread separately. With 621 orphaned threads, those commits added about 2.2–2.4 seconds to final reconciliation in the stress fixture.

## Change

Group shutdown recovery for up to 32 threads in one transaction. Each thread's events, command receipt, outbox changes, and projections remain atomic. Recovery reads and decides on the writer so later threads in a group see earlier updates, including shared session changes. Cancellation notifications run after the group's commit. Startup recovery keeps its existing per-thread behavior.

## Scope and approval

This is maintainer-directed work to fix measured shutdown overhead. It is a small, focused fix for an obvious performance defect: recovery opened and committed a separate transaction for every stale provider thread, even though ordered recovery can safely share the existing transaction wrapper. It changes only the recovery service and its regression tests, adds no product behavior or settings, and preserves SQLite durability and per-command persistence semantics. No separate feature proposal is needed for this fix.

## Verification

All 150 focused tests passed, and `vp run check:changed` passed, including 78 tests across four files, formatting, lint, knip, GraphQL checks, and affected package typechecks. Tests cover rollback, retry, duplicate calls, shared sessions, and notifications after commit. Benchmarks showed a benefit for orphan-heavy cleanup; small and his [...]

Final runtime reconciliation makes eleven database requests per candidate conversation.

This change combines the ten recovery collections into one SQLite statement, leaving the initial thread lookup separate. The collection filters, ordering and decoding stay the same. Conversations still reconcile in order and read fresh state after prior commits.

This PR implements the maintainer-requested investigation of final shutdown reconciliation. Its scope is limited to batching existing recovery reads and testing their selection, ordering and idempotency. Provider shutdown ordering, timeouts, selected data and recovery writes are unchanged. > [!NOTE]

Settings descriptions wrapped far too early. A description slightly longer than one line split into two half-width lines, leaving a big empty gap before the switch. On smaller windows, every Labs row ran to 3–5 lines. Two things caused it in `SettingsRow`:

- New lint rule `t3code/max-settings-description-length` caps a `SettingsRow` description at 200 characters of static text, including link text. The column holds about 110 characters per line next to a dropdown, so 200 stays two lines at normal window widths.

title: fix(server): prepare restart continuations faster on shutdown
author: Yash-Singh1
head: d173bbd0ab8e8416389c0cea3d7e8baa7ce5db80
body:
## Problem

Shutdown scanned every runtime thread and loaded full request history for attached threads before checking which records still needed cleanup. On populated databases, those reads slowed restart preparation and provider-session release.

## Change

Discover restart candidates from provider-session and run projections, filter by project continuation settings, and prepare eligible threads with concurrency limited to two. During session release, load pending requests first, then fetch only their nodes and turn items. Preserve the existing shutdown phases and durable write ordering.

## Scope and approval

This focused server performance fix narrows database reads used by existing shutdown and restart behavior. It adds no user-facing setting or workflow.

## Verification

Focused tests and affected-package typechecks passed. `vp run check:changed` passed.

On isolated populated fixtures, median request-cleanup time fell from 361 ms to 78 ms across three runs. With 625 restart candidates, preparation fell from 595 ms to 24 ms and read 4 conversations instead of 625. Total cleanup in that stress fixture remained about 3.87 seconds because final reconciliation dominated. Full desktop quit and process-exit latency were not measured.

title: fix(server): keep writes moving with a larger WAL limit
author: Yash-Singh1
head: 4d5f542832945ffb2d81ad0714ab8544848fe13c
body:
## Problem

A long-lived reader can hold an older WAL snapshot while writes continue. At the previous WAL limit, checkpoint backpressure could stall writes before that reader released its snapshot.

## Change

Raise the WAL size limit from 32 MiB to 128 MiB and allow backpressure up to 32,768 frames. Add a persistence test that holds a reader snapshot while writing a 48 MiB payload, then confirms another write completes before the reader releases its snapshot.

## Scope and approval

This is a focused fix for writer stalls caused by checkpoint backpressure when a reader retains a WAL snapshot.

## Verification

Added a focused persistence test covering a held reader snapshot, a WAL larger than the previous 10,000-frame backpressure threshold, and a subsequent successful write. The thread digest does not include the test run result.

title: perf(server): batch queued provider writes without waiting
author: Yash-Singh1
head: 8e9fefa7e05693c0835e595bc64d732741b3ce20
body:
## Problem

Provider snapshots commit separately even when several runs queue updates together. The fixed collection window reduced transaction overhead under load, but deliberately delayed isolated updates and used more CPU for sparse traffic. Writes should start as soon as the writer can process them and share transactions when updates are already queued.

## Change

Use one shared queue across provider runs and drain only the work already available, with no collection timer. Batching is enabled by default. Transactions remain bounded by 64 work items and 1 MiB of serialized snapshots; oversized snapshots run alone. All snapshots are preserved, and normalization sees preceding writes in the transaction.

Shared batches use per-job savepoints so a bad snapshot rolls back its own writes and deferred publications. Single-item batches use their outer transaction without a redundant savepoint. Transaction failures remain authoritative, while caller errors keep their identity. EOF acknowledgements do not open empty transactions. Ordinary writes use their direct path when no provider work is pending.

Controls execute on their consumer after preceding snapshots flush, preserving per-stream order without holding the shared worker while acquiring thread locks or checking background work. title: fix(web): keep the folder path caret in place while editing
author: juliusmarminge
head: 18e27bcf42e7e9bce4de2cd14331dcdb3e4c8b34
body:
## Problem

In Add project → Local folder, editing near the start of the path moves the caret to the end. On Windows, deleting the drive letter (`C:\Users\…` → `:\Users\…`) and typing a new one sends the new letter to the end of the path. On Linux the same thing happens when you delete the leading `/` of `/tmp/project`: the caret jumps from 0 to 11, and the next `/` you type produces `tmp/project/`.

## Change

The palette keys `CommandPaletteContent` on whether the query is a browse path. That remount resets Base UI's highlight state when the input switches between search and folder browsing, so it stays. An edit that briefly makes the text stop being a path flips that state, which remounts the input and loses the caret.

`handleQueryChange` now records the input's selection when a typed edit is about to flip browse mode. `CommandPaletteContent` restores it on the new input from its mount ref, and only when the new input's value matches. View pushes, back navigation, folder navigation and programmatic query changes are not recorded, so they behave as before. Arrow keys, Enter and highlight handling are unchanged.

## Scope and approval

Fixes pingdotgg/t3code#31610

## Verification

- Reproduced on main in the web dev server, on a fresh database with a Linux server. `/tmp/project`, caret after `/`, Backspace: the caret moved to the end and the typed `/` was appended (`tmp/project/`). Control: `~/wt/project`, Backspace after `~`, gives `/wt/project`. That is still a path, so  [...]

**Map the selection through path normalization.**

When a user pastes `/tmp/a\ b/` before `project`, `resolvePastedPath` removes the escape character, but the saved offset still refers to the unnormalized input. The restored caret lands after the `p`, so subsequent typing changes `project` at the wrong position. Map the offsets to `resolvedQuery` before saving them. title: perf(server): stop tracing the per-event background-work probe
author: juliusmarminge
head: 0b49b8d8f3e983807bacddfe924581b68a7225cc
body:
`RunExecutionService` ends a run's provider event stream with `Stream.takeUntilEffect(() => shouldStopProviderEventIngestion)`. Once the root turn has settled while background work (a dev server, a background terminal) keeps running, that check calls `session.hasPendingBackgroundWorkForThread` on every provider event. Codex and Claude wrapped the probe in a named `Effect.fn`, so each event exported a span.

Fleet telemetry for the 24h ending 2026-11-05 09:00 (nightly 4138):

| host | `CodexAdapterV2.hasPendingBackgroundWorkForThread` spans | p95 |
|---|---|---|
| cups | 338,052 (about 16k/h over 21h) | <1 ms |
| nucbox-1 | 405 | <1 ms |
| fs-42/43 (dev + nightly) | 158 | <1 ms |

On cups, one run's trace held 7,007 of these spans and grew past Tempo's 5 MB trace limit, so that trace can no longer be opened. The probe itself is cheap. The cost is span allocation, export bandwidth, and traces nobody can read.

Both probes now use `Effect.fnUntraced`, the convention for per-event code. Pi and OpenCode already used plain functions. The provider-switch and idle-unload callers still record their own spans (`Orchestrator.sessionHasBackgroundWork`, `ProviderSessionManager.unloadIdleThread`).

title: fix(mobile): iPad composer drops when the keyboard floats or minimizes
author: juliusmarminge
head: 3540949a748b11b326ec039a36e4a73e95d28c99
body:
## Problem

On iPad, when the keyboard stops being a docked keyboard, the thread composer stays lifted at the docked keyboard's height and leaves an empty band under it. The reporter hit this by floating the keyboard bar into the small pill at the bottom right; it stays wrong until the app is switched away from and back.

Reproduced on main (b28bb8fc9d) on an iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) simulator running iPadOS 26: open a thread, tap the composer, then press the keyboard's hide key while the composer keeps focus. iPadOS 26 leaves its minimized keyboard. UIKit first posts `keyboardWillShow` with a full-width 68.5pt frame at the bottom of the screen, then moves the keyboard with a duration-0 `keyboardWillChangeFrame` to `{y 1206, h 66, w 1032}`, which ends above the 1376pt screen bottom, and never posts `keyboardWillHide`. The composer stays lifted by about 60pt over empty space, even after it loses focus.

## Change

Every keyboard consumer in the mobile app (the composer's `KeyboardStickyView`, the chat list inset, `useKeyboardState`) is fed by react-native-keyboard-controller's iOS `KeyboardMovementObserver`. That observer only listens to `keyboardWillShow` and `keyboardWillHide`, and takes the end frame's height whether or not the keyboard is docked. Upstream 1.22.9 and upstream main behave the same way.

The existing pnpm patch for react-native-keyboard-controller 1.22.8 now also patches the observer:

- A keyboard counts as docked only when its end frame spans the screen width  [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Use the active app window as the geometry reference.**

`keyboardMetaData()` returns a screen-space frame. In Slide Over, that coordinate space differs from the app window. A docked keyboard can therefore be classified as floating by the current screen-width or screen-bottom checks. title: perf(mobile): stop iOS syntax highlighting from looking up a thread-local on every lexer call
author: camchis
head: af247c4e5ade7950e7315c4a3ecaed57184ba5ab
body:
## Problem

The @pierre/highlights lexer in `modules/t3-highlights` is WebAssembly compiled to C by wasm2c. wasm2c counts call depth to catch runaway recursion, and every generated function bumps a counter on entry and exit. Under C11, `wasm-rt.h` declares that counter `_Thread_local`. On Apple platforms each access to it then goes through `_tlv_get_addr`, a function call, so every lexer function entry pays for one.

## Fix

The pod's C files compile as `gnu99` (`GCC_C_LANGUAGE_STANDARD`). Without C11, `wasm-rt.h` defines `WASM_RT_THREAD_LOCAL` as empty on Apple platforms: upstream already disables `__thread` there. The counter becomes a plain global. That is safe because the lexer is already not reentrant: `t3_highlights.h` requires callers to serialize it, and `HybridT3Highlights` does so with a process-wide mutex.

The vendored sources compile unchanged as gnu99. The runtime's other thread-locals in this build, the saved stack depth (`wasm_rt_saved_call_stack_depth`) and the trap `jmp_buf`, are likewise touched only inside a lexer call. Its segment cache and alternate signal stack are compiled only for x86 segment registers and signal-based stack exhaustion, neither of which this build uses.

Android is untouched by this change. It builds the same C through CMake, where wasm2c's fallback is `__thread`. With minSdk 24 that becomes emulated TLS (`__emutls_get_address`), a similar cost that would need a different fix.

title: perf(server): provider-thread reads start from owned rows, not every node of the thread
author: juliusmarminge
head: be0c8ea08cea246e1d1eb146f53adbf969d5cca5
body:
Every MCP call from a thread (`OrchestratorMcpService.loadCaller`) and every `getThreadRecords` that includes provider threads reads the caller's provider threads with:

```sql
OR owner_node_id IN (SELECT node_id FROM orchestration_v2_projection_nodes WHERE thread_id = ?)
```

SQLite materializes that list from every node of the thread, so the cost grows with thread history. On personal hosts this statement was over 150 ms 86 times in the last 24 h (nightly 4138, max 2.4 s cold on cups). Almost all of them came from `OrchestratorMcpService.loadCaller → getThreadRecords → readCanonicalProjection` during cross-machine delegation. Neither DB below has a single provider thread with an owner, so the whole cost buys nothing.

The fix starts from provider threads that have an owner and checks the owner's thread by primary key, which is how the shell's provider-history read already does it (`ProjectionStore.ts`, "Start with non-null owners"). That subquery is now one fragment, used by the canonical read and the three point lookups (approval, run control, checkpoint rollback). The point lookups were already fast when `thread_id = ?` matched, but they no longer read all nodes when a subagent's provider thread misses it.

The delivery-identities test now covers a provider thread owned by a node of the thread that belongs to another app thread. No existing test reached the owner branch: the new assertion fails when that branch matches nothing and passes on `main` and with this change.

# [...]

** Minor** · **Performance & Scalability** · **Quick win**

**Use a correlated owner lookup for the three point reads.**

When many unrelated provider threads have non-null `owner_node_id` values, `nodesOwningProviderThreads` scans those owner rows even though the point reads already select one `provider_thread_id`. Use a correlated lookup from the selected provider-thread row to `orchestration_v2_projection_nodes.node_id`, with the existing `thread_id` check.

Keep the owner-first helper for the canonical read. The canonical read has no provider-thread target, and changing it to the point-read form could reintroduce the settled-node-history scan. This is a narrow scaling concern for the three point reads, not a demonstrated major regression.

title: perf(server): each live event is projected once for all subscribers
author: navidnadali
head: a8144903c5fc0a2f1a09ad9374751ed964e32271
body:
## Problem

Each live orchestration event is projected for the wire once per subscriber: `EventSink` builds a new projected object for every subscription (`project: (stored) => ({ ...stored, event: projectDomainEventForWire(stored.event) })`), the WebSocket thread stream wraps each event in a new stream item per subscriber, and the guest share stream projects the already projected event a second time. Every subscriber therefore gets its own copy, so `LiveStreamBudget`'s serialised-size cache never hits and each subscriber measures each event again. #28418 already removed the second projection in `ws.ts`; this is the rest.

## Change

- `projectStoredEventForWire` keeps one projection per stored event (a `WeakMap` keyed on the event object the PubSub hands every subscriber), and `threadStreamEventItem` shares one stream item per event.
- `EventSink`, the WebSocket thread stream and the guest share stream use them, so every subscriber receives the same object and the budget sizes it once.
- Consumers must not mutate the shared object (documented at the call site).

Wire output is unchanged. Server only; no client or contract change.

## Scope and approval

No product behaviour, default, setting or contract change. The cache is keyed on object identity and released with the event, so nothing can go stale. Overlap: #28418 (the `ws.ts` half, already on `main`).

Background and measurements: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/31002 (context, not an approval request).

title: fix(server): agents read RTF paragraphs that end with a backslash
author: geezoria
head: b474297b688f4f1e20fc084852eb91b1baba02d8
body:
## Problem

When a user attaches an `.rtf` file, the server extracts its text so the agent can read it. A document saved by macOS TextEdit reaches the agent as a single run-on paragraph.

The RTF spec treats a backslash followed by a carriage return or line feed as `\par`, and TextEdit ends every paragraph that way:

```rtf
\f0\fs24 \cf0 First\
Second\
Third}
```

The `rtf()` reader in `documentTextWorker.ts` skipped the pair as an unknown control symbol, so the agent received `FirstSecondThird`. An explicit `\par` in the same position already yields a newline. The agent loses the paragraph, list and line structure of the document it was asked to read.

## Change

In the reader's control-symbol branch, a backslash before `\n` or `\r` now yields the same `"\n"` that `\par` yields, and respects hidden destinations in the same way. For `\`, the `\r` is consumed with the backslash, and the loop already skips the bare `\n` that follows, so CRLF files give one newline, not two.

## Scope and approval

This is a very small, focused fix for an obvious bug, so it uses CONTRIBUTING's exception for those. It is a one-line parsing correction for a form the RTF spec defines and macOS TextEdit writes. Documents that use `\par` are unchanged.

It is the agent-facing counterpart of #30812, which fixes the same rule in the web file preview's separate RTF parser. The two readers share no code and either fix stands alone, so they are separate PRs as CONTRIBUTING asks.

author: navidnadali
head: 89f399b77db0668a6944a28e31e9807f79e699d3
body:
## Problem

A thread has one root checkpoint scope, which every root run re-creates with its own node, time and cwd. A stopped run's checkpoint is captured by an effect after the run ends. A message sent after Stop, or queued during the run, can re-create the scope first, and the capture then records its baselines with the next run's node and time. ## Change

The baselines a capture writes take the captured run's own root node and request time, not the scope's current ones. Two files: `CheckpointCaptureService.ts` and `CheckpointService.ts`. Server only; no client or contract change.

title: fix(shared): preserve IPv6 hosts when switching clone protocols
author: Lucenx9
head: 2287ce49ea47dddaabb54f00154d41ba830e2d8d
body:
## Problem

Switching `git@[2001:db8::1]:org/repo.git` to HTTPS produces `https://[2001/db8::1]:org/repo.git`, which is not a valid URL. The SCP matcher splits at the first colon inside the IPv6 address, while the URI matchers reject bracketed hosts. The shared helper feeds the server's existing HTTPS retry after SSH rejection and the client's protocol selector.

## Change

Treat a bracketed host as one token in the SCP-style, SSH URI and HTTP(S) URI patterns. Keep the existing port guard, credentials handling and path spelling. Exclude square brackets from the plain SCP host alternative so an absolute-path bracketed remote cannot backtrack into a partial host. Extend the existing conversion/refusal tests.

## Scope and approval

This is a very small, focused obvious-bug fix: valid Git remotes are misparsed by an established protocol conversion operation. Only the shared parser and adjacent test change, with no setting, product default, dependency or diagnostic suppression.

The IPv6 problem was also noted in #27845. A [maintainer explicitly separated it from that password fix](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/27845#issuecomment-6549522895); that comment is scope context, not approval of this implementation. The targeted duplicate audit inspected changed-file lists for 418 candidate open PRs and relevant source in 12 related PRs, including #27845, #24886 and #24904. None contains this IPv6 repair. This is a targeted check, not an exhaustive guarantee.

## Verification [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Reject bracketed absolute-path SCP hosts in the plain-host alternative.**

`git@[2001:db8::1]:/srv/repo.git` is a valid Git SCP form. The new bracketed alternative fails on the leading `/`, so the plain-host alternative matches the partial host `[2001`. The result is an HTTPS URL with the wrong host, `https://[2001/db8::1]:/srv/repo.git`. That URL is offered as the HTTPS option in the clone dialog and used by the HTTPS retry, and it cannot reach the intended host. Absolute-path SCP inputs are already refused for non-bracketed hosts, so this input should also be refused.

✅ Addressed in commit 2287ce4

title: fix(client-runtime): sanitized error stacks keep line and column for URLs with a query
author: geezoria
head: b7ad186e86f3afb62b3abeacf5c6055e077d9018
body:
## Problem

`safeErrorLogAttributes` is supposed to keep a client error's stack frames while it strips credentials, query strings and fragments from the frame URLs. When a frame's URL has a query string or fragment, the frame's `:line:column` is lost too.

The frame regex captures the URL together with its trailing position. For `react-dom_client.js?v=4f2a91c3:12345:17`, `new URL` parses `:12345:17` as part of the query, so `url.search = ""` deletes the position along with it:

```
at commitRoot (http://localhost:5173/node_modules/.vite/deps/react-dom_client.js?v=4f2a91c3:12345:17)
→ at commitRoot (http://localhost:5173/node_modules/.vite/deps/react-dom_client.js)
```

Every Vite dev module (`?v=`, `?t=`), every Metro bundle frame (`index.bundle?platform=ios&dev=true:1234:56`), and Firefox-style `fn@url?query:line:col` frames lose their positions. The logged stack can't point at a line. Frames without a query keep their positions, so the behaviour is inconsistent with the sanitizer's own intent.

## Change

Before clearing the search and fragment, `sanitizeStackUrl` takes a trailing `:line[:column]` from whichever of the two it is about to remove, and appends it to the sanitized URL. Only digits and colons are carried over. Credentials, query and fragment are still removed. The position is read from the query or fragment rather than from the whole URL, so a bare `host:port` is never mistaken for a position.

title: fix(shared): command output no longer prints the final byte of escape sequences with intermediates
author: geezoria
head: aed463bda909b093689215c9ad9fe4c1149153a1
body:
## Problem

The shared command-output parser prints part of some valid escape sequences as text. `escapeLength` treats only `ESC (`, `ESC )`, `ESC *` and `ESC +` as three-byte sequences, and cuts every other escape at two bytes. Any other sequence with intermediate bytes therefore loses its final byte into the visible output:

- `ESC # 8` (DECALN)
- `ESC % G` (select UTF-8)
- `ESC SP F` (S7C1T)
- the 96-character set designators `ESC - A` and `ESC . A`
- multi-byte designators such as `ESC ( % 5`

For example, `before ESC#8 after` renders as `before8after`.

ECMA-35 (section 13) and ECMA-48 (section 5.3) define an escape sequence as `ESC`, then any number of intermediate bytes in 0x20–0x2F, then one final byte in 0x30–0x7E. The existing comment shows the charset case was meant to be handled this way, but only four of the designators were covered.

## Change

`escapeLength` now consumes every intermediate byte after `ESC` and then the one final byte. While a sequence is still unfinished at the end of a chunk, it keeps returning `-1` to wait for more input, as before. Two-byte sequences such as `ESC 7`, `ESC 8` and `ESC M`, and the existing `ESC ( B` / `ESC ) 0` designations, produce the same lengths as before. CSI and string sequences are unchanged. Only 0x30–0x7E can be the final byte. If a control or a new `ESC` follows the intermediates, the sequence ends before it and that byte is processed normally. So `ESC # ESC [31m` still applies the colour and `ESC # LF` keeps the new [...]

title: fix(server): ACP MCP bridge no longer splits messages on U+2028/U+2029
author: geezoria
head: 2e70711664d5b57d5fa46606eedb897868742617
body:
## Problem

ACP agents reach T3 Code's MCP tools through `t3 acp-mcp-bridge`, which frames stdin with `node:readline`. Readline also ends a line at U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR). `JSON.stringify` leaves both characters raw inside strings, and MCP stdio clients send messages that way: the official SDK writes `JSON.stringify(message) + "\n"` and splits only on `\n`.

So when a tool call's arguments contain either character, for example text pasted from a PDF, Word document, or web page, the bridge cuts the message into fragments. It answers each fragment with a `-32700 Parse error` that has `id: null`, and never forwards the request. Because the agent never gets a reply carrying its request id, the tool call hangs until the agent's own timeout.

## Change

Frame stdin with `Stream.decodeText` and `Stream.splitLines` instead of `node:readline`. `splitLines` ends lines at `\n`, `\r\n` and a lone `\r`, the same terminators readline used, but not at U+2028/U+2029. `provider-pi`'s RPC reader avoids readline for the same reason (`packages/provider-pi/src/server/rpc.ts:1`).

- A trailing `\r` and a final unterminated line are still handled as before.
- Multi-byte characters split across chunks still decode correctly, because `decodeText` streams.
- The bridge no longer imports a Node built-in, so the `nodeBuiltinImport:off` directive is removed.

## Scope and approval

This is a very small, focused fix for an obvious bug, so it uses CONTRIBUTING's exception  [...]

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Split on LF only.**

Effect 4.1.2 also treats a standalone `\r` as a delimiter. A valid LF-delimited message such as `{"jsonrpc":"2.0",\r"id":1,"method":"tools/list"}\n` is therefore split and rejected. This behavior existed with `readline`, but remains inconsistent with the requested LF-only framing. Use an LF-only framer and add this case to the bridge test. ([effect.website](https://effect.website/docs/v4/api/effect/Stream/))

title: fix(server): rewound Codex threads import their history from before the rewind
author: MarcoDotIO
head: aa39d17803651276d8c850edae0b4eef7c200f0b
body:
## Problem

Codex reverts a paginated thread (Codex Desktop rewind, `thread/revert`) by writing a new, immutable rollout named `rollout--_.jsonl`. Its `session_meta.history_base` points at the rollout it replaces, `{ thread_id: , end_byte_offset }`, and the new file inherits that file's first `end_byte_offset` bytes (see `revert_thread.rs` and `paginated_fork.rs` in `codex-rs/thread-store/src/local/`). Repeated rewinds form a chain of rollouts.

Onboarding import (`/welcome` → `agentSessions.import` → `AgentSessionScanner.recentThreads`) reads each rollout on its own. The newest one sorts first and is imported. Every earlier rollout of the thread has the same session ID, so it is then dropped as a duplicate. As a result, the imported thread starts at the last rewind and loses everything before it, without the "earlier messages were not imported" notice. On a real Codex Desktop home, one thread was split across five rollouts after four rewinds. Import kept only the last one.

## Change

When a Codex rollout has a `history_base`, `recentThreads` follows the chain through the earlier rollouts it found during the scan. It reads each inherited prefix, keeps the shared 32 MiB history budget and the import byte budget, and parses those records ahead of the new ones. It drops the inherited `session_meta` records, so the rollout's own metadata still names the thread. `readTranscript` gains an optional byte limit for these prefix reads. title: fix(opencode): edits that delete text keep their empty replacement
author: Jo2234
head: 513097fefa714ef86334d4e0659a9e2e6f0e3100
body:
## Problem

OpenCode's file-change projection (`packages/provider-opencode/src/server/toolItems.ts`) reads `oldString`/`newString`/`content` through `recordString`, which treats any string whose `trim()` is empty as missing. So an OpenCode edit that deletes text (`newString: ""`), a whitespace-only replacement, or an empty-file write loses its recorded before/after text. When no usable patch metadata is present, the tool-call Open diff path (`apps/web/src/lib/toolCallDiff.ts`) shows recorded before/after content, so the deletion's after-state goes missing. An empty preferred key could also fall through to a later alias key. Other adapters already keep exact strings: Muse's tests expect `newStr: ""`, and ACP and Pi keep every string.

## Fix

Use an exact-string reader only for `oldStr` and `newStr`. It takes the first key whose value is a string, including an empty one. Paths, labels, commands and patch selection keep their existing non-empty validation. The OpenCode v1 and v2 adapters both use this mapper.

title: fix(server): an invalid regex in project search still finds its text when Match case is off
author: MarcoDotIO
head: 2e9a9c9be82403f064846ae7c90303d7c192fb8f
body:
## Problem

In project content search, "Use regular expression" on with "Match case" off (the default) gave no results for a pattern that does not compile, such as `foo(`. With "Match case" on, the same pattern still listed the literal `foo(` matches below the "Invalid regular expression" notice.

Call path: `ProjectContentSearchDialog` → `projects.searchContents` (`ws.ts`) → `WorkspaceEntries.searchContents` → `WorkspaceSearchIndex.searchContents`. For a case-insensitive regex search, `buildContentSearchQuery` sends fff `(?i)`. When the pattern fails to compile, fff sets `regexFallbackError` and searches the pattern as a literal. That literal is `(?i)foo(`, prefix included, so nothing matches.

## Change

When a case-insensitive regex search comes back with `regexFallbackError`, `searchContents` keeps the error and runs the search again as a plain, case-insensitive literal search: the same query the dialog sends with regex off. Case-sensitive searches are unchanged, because fff's own literal fallback already gives them the right results.

## Scope and approval

This is a small fix for an obvious bug: one search mode returned nothing where the matching mode returned results. It touches one function in the server's search index and adds one test. Contracts and clients are unchanged, and `regexFallbackError` is still reported, so the "Invalid regular expression" notice still shows.

## Before and after

Web dev client, project content search with regex on and Match case off, se [...]

**Keep the regex error when the indexed prefilter finds no candidates.**

When the content index is ready, an invalid case-insensitive pattern such as `foo(` is searched as `(?i)foo(`. fff's bigram prefilter keeps only files that contain every bigram of that literal. If no indexed file contains those bigrams, `grep_search` can return an empty result before it records the compile error. The retry at `WorkspaceSearchIndex.ts:505` then does not run, and the result has no `regexFallbackError`. The UI shows no results and no invalid-regex notice.

title: fix(server): a branch tracking another local branch no longer shows that branch's PR
author: MarcoDotIO
head: 6e79ab717f4a49cddbc8013212ad3cb12a948c79
body:
## Problem

A branch that tracks another local branch gets that branch's PR. `git switch -c feature --track develop` records `branch.feature.remote = .`. T3's own `createRef` does the same under `branch.autoSetupMerge=always`. `GitManager.branchPullRequest` read the saved upstream (`.` plus `refs/heads/develop`) as the published head and listed PRs with `--head develop`. If `develop` had an open `develop -> main` PR, that PR came back as the feature branch's PR.

`branchPullRequest` feeds `ThreadPullRequestService`, which links the thread to the PR, and `ThreadSettlementService`. So a feature thread was linked to the release PR and settled when that PR merged. The call path is `lookupBranchPullRequest` → `resolveLookupHeadContext` → `resolveBranchHeadContext`, which takes `extractBranchNameFromRemoteRef("./develop", { remoteName: "." })` and gets `develop`. `develop` is not the default branch, so the existing guard for a default-branch base does not apply.

Reproduce in a repo with an `origin`:

```sh
git switch -c develop && git push -u origin develop   # develop has an open PR into main
git switch -c feature --track develop                 # branch.feature.remote = .
```

The feature thread now links to the `develop` PR.

## Change

A branch remote of `.` now counts as "no remote" in `resolveBranchHeadContext` and in `resolvePrLookupRepositoryIdentity`. The second one keeps the identity check consistent: without it, the lookup would fail with "Repository identity could not  [...]

title: fix(cli): t3 project remove finds a deleted project by a relative or trailing-slash path
author: MarcoDotIO
head: c42609dedad8a5d1f6ac714e225e14793c8cc27e
body:
## Problem

After a project's folder is deleted, `t3 project remove` and `t3 project rename` find it only by the exact stored absolute path. A relative path or a path with a trailing slash reports "No active project found", even though the same spelling works while the folder exists:

```sh
cd ~/code && rm -rf old-app
t3 project remove old-app        # No active project found for 'old-app'.
t3 project remove ~/code/old-app/  # No active project found for '/Users/me/code/old-app/'.
```

Call path: `projectRemoveCommand` / `projectRenameCommand` → `findActiveProjectTarget` (`apps/server/src/cli/project.ts`) → `WorkspacePaths.normalizeWorkspaceRoot`. Normalizing does `path.resolve` plus home expansion, then stats the directory. When the directory is missing it fails with `WorkspaceRootNotExistsError`, and the lookup fell back to comparing the raw identifier with the stored paths. Stored paths are always resolved and absolute, so only an exact absolute spelling could match. #9885 added that fallback for the stored path. This change extends it to every spelling that resolves to the stored path.

## Change

Every `normalizeWorkspaceRoot` failure already carries the resolved `normalizedWorkspaceRoot`. The lookup now matches against that value instead of the raw identifier, so a missing folder resolves the same way an existing one does. Looking up by project ID comes first and is unchanged. Symlink aliases are still not resolved for missing folders, just as before. `ProjectNotFoundEr [...]

** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win**

**Reject parent-traversal fallbacks when normalization fails.**

When `/a/link` is a symlink, `/a/link/../foo` can identify a different filesystem location from lexical `/a/foo`. If `/a/foo` is a registered missing project, the new fallback selects it, and `remove --force` can delete that project’s threads.

Reject failed-normalization fallbacks that contain a `..` path segment. Preserve normalized matching for successful paths and for relative or trailing-slash inputs without parent traversal.

body:
## Problem

GitLab merge requests offered no "Request changes" verdict, and changes requested on GitLab never showed in T3. The capability comment said GitLab has no such verdict, which hasn't been true since GitLab added reviewer review states. Closes #30548.

## Change

- The GitLab provider now offers `request-changes`. Web and mobile already show the option when the capability lists it.
- `submitReview` sends the verdict with the `mergeRequestRequestChanges` GraphQL mutation, after the comments and summary like approve. GitLab keeps the state on a reviewer and answers "Reviewer not found" otherwise, so it first appends the viewer with `mergeRequestSetReviewers(operationMode: APPEND)`. Appending someone who is already a reviewer keeps their state.
- GitLab answers a refused mutation with HTTP 200 and the reasons in the payload's `errors`. A new `GitLabMutationRefusedError` carries them, so the UI shows GitLab's reason instead of failing silently.
- The approval read now also asks for each reviewer's `reviewState`. Any `REQUESTED_CHANGES` makes the decision `changes-requested`, ahead of approvals. That gives GitLab rows the list's "Changes requested" icon and makes the review filter match them.
- On servers whose reviewers have no `reviewState`, that GraphQL query fails as a whole. The read then retries without it, so older servers keep their approval badges.

title: fix(mobile): iOS terminal accepts Chinese, Japanese and Korean input
author: juliusmarminge
head: 633c291227edf0d860360541073ce594a8489fbc
body:
## Problem

The iOS app's native terminal can't type Chinese, Japanese or Korean. Its hidden input field is `.asciiCapable`, so iOS offers only the English keyboard there: no globe key, and Pinyin, Kana and Hangul can't be selected. Its delegate sent every keystroke to the PTY at once and rejected the change, so an IME could never compose either. Reproduced on main (`66e6217b93`) on an iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 27.2: with 简体拼音 added in Settings, the chat composer lists it under the globe key, but the terminal shows only English, and tapping `n i h a o` sends the raw `nihao` to the shell.

## Change

All of this is in `apps/mobile/modules/t3-terminal/ios/T3TerminalView.swift`, unless noted otherwise.

- **Keyboards:** the field uses `.default`. Autocorrection, spell checking, smart punctuation and smart insert stay off.
- **When input is sent:** UIKit owns marked text. Input goes to the PTY from `.editingChanged` only when nothing is marked, so a composition sends only its committed result.
- **Keys during a composition:**
  - Backspace edits the marked text and sends no DEL.
  - Return (確定 / Confirm) commits it and sends no CR.
  - The hardware key commands (arrows, Tab, Escape, Ctrl) are withdrawn, so they drive the candidates.
- **Korean:** the iOS Korean keyboard builds a syllable by replacing the committed character before the cursor and uses no marked text. So the field keeps committed text and sends each change as one DEL per replaced character plus the new suffix. ㅎ [...]

## Problem

The command output an agent's tool call streams into a thread loses text after an unterminated OSC. A program that sets a title with `ESC ]0;title` and then prints `ESC [31m` before it sends BEL or `ESC \` has the rest of the line swallowed into the title string, so `printf '\033]0;title\033\033[31mred\033[0m\n'` shows an empty line instead of `red`.

A second ESC right after an ESC now restarts the sequence, so it is no longer read as a two-byte escape that eats the ESC of the CSI after it. A string that is still open at the end of a chunk is held as before, so a payload split across chunks stays hidden.

The parser is shared. The fold runs in the server's `CommandOutputHub` (normalised and resume text) and in `packages/client-runtime/src/state/commandOutput.ts` (`appendTerminalOutput`, which web and mobile use); web's `CommandOutputPanel` and mobile's command output then render its spans. The integrated terminal (PTY) does not use this parser and is unchanged.

title: fix(gitlab): merge requests can delete their source branch
author: TonybynMp4
head: cc09949bc7f668642eb14d69ef7a056cb327edb5
body:
## Problem

Closed and merged GitLab merge requests had no "Delete branch" action. The provider reported `deleteBranch: false` and never listed `delete-branch`. Closes #30452.

## Change

- The detail read of a closed or merged merge request asks GitLab for `userPermissions.removeSourceBranch` and keeps `delete-branch` in the viewer's actions only when it is true. GitLab sets it to false once the branch is gone, so a merge request whose branch was already removed shows no action.
- `delete-branch` runs in the source project, which matters for forks. Before deleting, it reads the merge request again and refuses if it is open, if the viewer can't remove the branch, if the branch is the project's default branch, or if the branch head moved past the merge request head. Each refusal is a typed `GitLabBranchDeletionRefusedError` with its own message.
- The provider capability is now `deleteBranch: true`.

GitHub's delete is a compare-and-swap on the ref. GitLab's branch delete endpoint takes no expected SHA, so a push landing between the head check and the `DELETE` can still be lost. The comment in `deleteSourceBranch` says so.

## Scope and approval

GitLab adapter only, plus `delete-branch` in the shared GitLab action list. No contract change. Web and mobile already gate the action on the capability and the viewer's actions. Tracked in #30452.

## Verification

** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Heavy lift**

**Delete the branch with an atomic SHA condition.**

If a push changes the branch after the SHA check to a commit with the same or an older author date, this header permits deletion of the new head. GitLab also checks the date before it calls the deletion service, rather than atomically with deletion. This can remove unmerged commits from the remote. ([gitlab.com](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab/-/raw/master/lib/api/branches.rb))

Use an atomic expected-SHA deletion, such as a Git push with an explicit `--force-with-lease`, or refuse deletion when that guarantee is unavailable. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push))

title: fix(gitlab): the checks and review list filters work
author: TonybynMp4
head: 6b2c076535d11e07c3d898bd0721e30ac546629d
body:
## Problem

Two of the pull request list's filters were broken for GitLab merge requests.

The checks filter did nothing. GitLab list rows carried no `checksState`, so the server's row filter skipped `checks`. Closes #30432.

The review filter only ran after the fetch, because GitLab's REST list can't filter by review state. GitLab returned a page of unfiltered merge requests and the server then dropped most of the rows. "Changes requested" or "Approved" could leave a page short or empty even when matching merge requests existed further down. GitLab also never reported "changes requested" at all: the decision came only from approvals.

## Change

Checks:

- The GraphQL read that already fetched approvals for up to 100 merge requests now also asks for `headPipeline { status }`. It maps the status with the same rules as the checks panel. Success is passing, failed or canceled is failing, and a running or waiting pipeline is pending. A manual or skipped pipeline, or no pipeline, gives `null` (no checks).
- `getReviewDecisions` is now `getListStates` and returns both values. Listed rows and the summary get `checksState` from it.
- `matchesRowFilters` in `PullRequestService` now applies `checks` too. Rows whose `checksState` is `undefined` pass, so hosts that don't report it behave as before.

Review:

- A reviewer whose `reviewState` is `REQUESTED_CHANGES` makes the merge request "changes requested". That outranks an approval, as on GitHub.
- On GitLab 17.9 and later, the list re [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Do not fall back to an offset REST read for a resumed GraphQL cursor.**

For `review: "changes-requested"`, GraphQL counts only matching rows, but REST uses `cursor.delivered` as an offset across all rows because REST has no equivalent filter. If the resumed GraphQL read fails, REST can return rows already emitted by GraphQL. Fail the resumed read instead of switching to an incompatible REST offset. Keep the REST fallback for an initial GraphQL read.

✅ Addressed in commit 242bff6

replies.body: Fixed in 242bff6440. Only a first GraphQL read falls back to REST now. A resumed read returns its error, and the CLI test covers that case.

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win**

**Log a bounded category instead of `error.cause`.**

The log annotation `cause: error.cause` carries the full schema decode failure. A schema failure message can embed the decoded GraphQL payload values. That text is unbounded and can include raw response content.

The nearby code uses `reason: error._tag` for the same kind of warning (the line-count read in this file and `listStates` in the provider). Use the same bounded fields here. The full error still exists as `cause` on the error value for callers that need it.

As per coding guidelines: "Attributes and log annotations stay bounded: no raw payloads, command arguments or output, signed URLs, credentials, query strings, or arbitrary defect text."

_Source: Coding guidelines_

✅ Addressed in commit 242bff6

replies.body: Fixed in 242bff6440. The warning logs `reason: error._tag`, the same as the other list warnings.

title: fix(gitlab): threads on changed code show as outdated
author: TonybynMp4
head: 24c575970bb1fe7e8638cea2da0c5292b531c1b1
body:
## Problem

The GitLab adapter set `isOutdated: false` on every review thread. After a push changed the line a thread was on, T3 Code still showed it as current, unlike GitLab's own UI and GitHub threads in T3 Code. Closes #30422.

## Change

GitLab moves a thread's position onto each new diff while its line still exists. So a thread is current only when its position's `base_sha`, `start_sha` and `head_sha` all match the merge request's `diff_refs`.

- The discussions decoder now keeps each text thread's position refs, and the CLI collects them across pages.
- The merge request detail decoder now reads `diff_refs`.
- `getChangeRequestActivity` compares the two. It reads the detail fresh rather than from the one-minute cache, because refs cached from before a push would mark every thread outdated. That adds one uncached detail request per activity read, including watcher polls. The same read also supplies the note links added in #30411, so the activity read makes one detail request in total.

If the detail read fails, or a thread has no refs, the thread stays current, as before.

## Scope and approval

Adapter only. Web already shows "Outdated" on the summary, timeline and code tabs. Mobile now leaves outdated GitLab threads out of the diff, as it does for GitHub, and labels them in the timeline and discussion screens. Tracked in #30422.

## Verification

- New tests fail on main and pass here: the detail decoder reads `diff_refs`, the CLI returns each thread's position refs,  [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Data Integrity & Integration** · **Quick win**

**Accept a partial `diff_refs` object without failing the merge-request detail.**

GitLab can return `diff_refs` with `base_sha: null` for an orphaned source branch. `RawMergeRequestSchema` decodes `diff_refs` with `RawDiffRefs`, which requires all three SHAs as strings. The whole merge-request decode then fails, so `mergeRequestDetail` returns `GitLabMergeRequestReadError`. This affects `getChangeRequest`, `getChangeRequestSummary`, `getChangeRequestChecks`, `getChangeRequestPreview`, and `getViewerPermissions`. Thread activity still loads, but its refs read falls back to `undefined`, so outdated threads show as current. This PR introduced the decode, so the failure is a regression.

Decode the merge-request field with a nullable schema. Treat an incomplete ref set as `null`, and omit `diffRefs` from the detail. Leave the standalone decoder and `GitLabDiffRefs` unchanged.

Also add a test case with a non-null `diff_refs` object whose `base_sha` is `null`. The current failure test covers only `diff_refs: null`.

✅ Confirmed as addressed by @TonybynMp4

replies.body: Fixed in 08e61d971b. The merge-request schema now decodes diff_refs with nullable SHAs, and toDetail drops an incomplete set, so the detail read succeeds and diffRefs is omitted. The decoder test covers base_sha: null.

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Keep discussion refs and merge-request refs from the same snapshot.**

The direct WebSocket and review-guide activity paths do not invalidate the GitLab detail cache. After a push, `getChangeRequestActivity` can therefore compare fresh discussions with pre-push `diffRefs`, causing both directions of incorrect outdated classification. The result can remain visible for up to 60 seconds through the service activity cache.

✅ Confirmed as addressed by @TonybynMp4

replies.body: Fixed in 08e61d971b. getChangeRequestActivity now reads the merge-request diff refs straight from the CLI instead of the cached detail, so they come from the same read as the discussions. The provider test primes the cache with stale refs first and still gets the current classification.

@TonybynMp4 The supplied code confirms that `getChangeRequestActivity` now calls `cli.getMergeRequestDetail` directly and preserves the `recoverRead` fallback. This addresses the stale-cache finding.

The discussions and diff refs still use separate requests, but neither uses the cached detail for this comparison.

author: TonybynMp4
head: 82fec15b2077b4c48ebf818129e6a1c9c543f4b1
body:
## Problem

GitLab comments never carried `editedAt`, so a bot that rewrites its comment in place never woke `watch_pull_request`. Closes #30402.

## Change

The reactions GraphQL query already walks every note on each activity read. Its note nodes now also ask for `lastEditedAt`, `lastEditedBy` and `resolved`, so there's no extra request. The provider sets `editedAt` on matching conversation and thread comments.

`lastEditedAt` can't be taken as is. Resolving or reopening a thread moves it on every note in the thread (see the transcript in #30402). That second rule covers a note edited once and resolved later, whose stamp would otherwise be the resolve.

What's left: reopening a thread that holds an edited note moves its stamp, so the watcher reports that note again once. Reopening is activity on the thread, so I left it.

Small fix. GitHub and Forgejo already set `editedAt`; this brings GitLab in line. Tracked in #30402.

title: perf(resource-monitor): Linux terminal process checks use a third of the CPU
author: jaikhuranna
head: 1569686cb8c71dc6abc308f0e1afa239046f085a
body:
## Problem

While a terminal session is running, the server asks the native resource monitor for the process table every second (`DEFAULT_SUBPROCESS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` in `apps/server/src/terminal/Manager.ts`) to tell whether the shell has a child process. On Linux the monitor builds a full sysinfo record for every process on the host to return three fields. sysinfo reads `/proc//stat` and also opens `/proc//status` for each process. On a desktop with ~480 processes, one call costs ~14 ms of CPU, so an open terminal keeps ~1.4% of a core busy.

## Change

On Linux, `process_table` reads pid, ppid and name straight from `/proc//stat`, the file sysinfo already takes them from. The name runs to the last `)`, so names with spaces or parentheses parse the same way. macOS, Windows and Android keep the sysinfo path. The server, the protocol and the polling cadence are unchanged.

```diff
 process_table()
-  sysinfo refresh_processes(All, nothing().without_tasks())
-    per pid: read stat, open status (tgid check), build Process
+  #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
+  per entry in /proc: read stat -> (name, ppid)
   sort by pid
```

## Scope and approval

This qualifies for the focused-fix exception: one recurring CPU cost in an existing path, with output identical to what the server receives today. It adds no setting, contract, cadence or behavior change. No maintainer approval is claimed. I found no open PR touching the resource monitor's process table.

title: fix(server): ACP agents get T3CODE_THREAD_ID like Claude and Codex sessions
author: frankhommers
head: 66536ae27ec6807b2e378550b74a8adf35291322
body:
## Problem

Claude sessions get `T3CODE_THREAD_ID` since #22542, and Codex sessions since #28604. Agents that run through the ACP layer (the ACP Registry agents such as Copilot CLI, claude-acp, Devin, Factory Droid, GLM and Mistral Vibe, plus local ACP executables) still do not: the per-thread process environment they are spawned with carries `T3_ACP_MCP_*`, but not the thread id.

So a process such an agent starts cannot find its T3 thread. ````

```

body:
## Problem

HTTP authentication schemes are case-insensitive (RFC 9110, section 11.1). #23782 made the `Bearer` parser follow that: `parseBearerToken` in `apps/server/src/auth/EnvironmentAuth.ts` matches `/^Bearer /i`. `parseDpopToken`, the next function in the file, still requires the exact prefix `DPoP `.

So a request with `Authorization: dpop ` and a valid `DPoP` proof matches neither parser. The server treats it as carrying no credential at all and refuses it with `ServerAuthMissingCredentialError`. The check in `apps/server/src/auth/http.ts` that adds the `WWW-Authenticate: DPoP` challenge to an unauthorized response has the same exact-prefix test.

No current client hits this. T3's own web, mobile and relay clients write `DPoP` exactly, and MCP clients use `Bearer`. This is the same conformance #23782 gave `Bearer`, applied to the other scheme the same credential selector reads, so any DPoP client that writes the scheme differently is accepted the way a `bearer` client already is.

## Change

`parseDpopToken` matches its scheme with `/^DPoP /i`, the same shape as `parseBearerToken`. The challenge check in `http.ts` uses the same pattern.

Token extraction, proof verification and the order credentials are tried in stay as they were. One consequence follows from the parser now seeing the header: a request that sends a session cookie together with `Authorization: dpop ` is judged on the DPoP credential, as a request with `Authorization: DPoP ` already is, instead of falli [...]

title: fix(server): message search keeps results when a short non-Latin word differs in case
author: MarcoDotIO
head: 6c9fa82fd2c3778da8d7894714ff5796ea80a0b8
body:
## Problem

Message search drops a thread when a short word in the query only appears in the message with different case or accents, if that word is not ASCII. Searching `ошибка в` does not find a message reading `В логах ошибка`, and `fermée éc` does not find `École fermée à Lyon`. The thread also disappears while typing: `ошибка ло` loses `Логи: ошибка` until the next letter makes the word long enough for the index.

Call path: the command palette, mobile search and `t3_thread_search` all reach `searchMessages` in `ThreadSearch.ts`. `buildMessageSearch` sends tokens shorter than three characters as `substrings`, and `messageHitsQuery` rejects a row when `instr(lower(text), token) = 0`. SQLite's `lower()` folds ASCII only, while `messageSearchTokens` lowercases with JavaScript, so `в` never equals `В` in SQL. `messageMatcher`, which ignores case and accents, never sees the row.

## Change

`buildMessageSearch` now checks each non-ASCII short token against the case and accent spellings it can match (`в` as `в` or `В`, `éc` as `éc`, `Éc`, `ec` and so on), with or without the index. Short tokens are at most two characters, so that is at most 16 spellings. The check stays in SQL so these tokens still narrow hits before the hit limit, and `messageMatcher` still decides the final match. ASCII short tokens stay in SQL, because they are what keep a rare short word from being cut off by the hit limit.

## Scope and approval

Small, focused fix of an obvious bug: one filter in one fun [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Apply the short-token match before the hit limit.**

For `ошибка в`, newer messages containing `ошибка` but not `в` can pass SQL after `в` is removed from `substrings`. They can fill `MESSAGE_HIT_LIMIT` before `messageMatcher` rejects them, so an older message containing both words can be omitted. The previous implementation applied the short-token SQL filter before the limit. Page through bounded candidates until enough rows pass `messageMatcher`, or apply an equivalent Unicode-aware filter before the limit. Add a regression case that exhausts the limit in both index modes.

✅ Addressed in commit 6c9fa82

Fixed in 6c9fa82fd2: each non-ASCII short token is now checked in SQL as the case and accent spellings it can match, so it narrows hits before the limit again and `messageMatcher` still decides the final match. A new test puts 2,000 newer long-word-only messages ahead of an older message with both words, with and without the index.

title: fix(cli): t3 connect unlink no longer warns about a server that is gone
author: MarcoDotIO
head: df37fad362909d233e6b4c44991c83d75734df4e
body:
## Problem

After a server dies without a clean shutdown (`kill -9`, OOM, power loss), `userdata/server-runtime.json` stays on disk. `t3 connect unlink` and `t3 connect logout` trust that record:

`connectUnlinkCommand` -> `disconnectCloud` -> `runLiveCloudUnlink` -> `readPersistedServerRuntimeState` -> `client.connect.unlink` against the recorded origin

Nothing checks that the recorded server still exists, which has two results:

- With nothing on the port, the request fails and the user sees "T3 Connect is disabled, but the running server could not stop its tunnel. Restart that server to stop the connector." There is no running server to restart, and the unlink actually worked.
- If another process has since taken the port, the CLI sends it a freshly minted `relay:write` bearer token, which stays valid until the command revokes it on exit. `t3 pair` guards against this exact case ("A dead server's port may be reused").

## Change

`runLiveCloudUnlink` now treats a record whose PID is dead as `server-gone`, using the `isProcessAlive` check that `t3 pair`, `t3 update` and `t3 policy` already use. The CLI mints no token, makes no request, and prints "T3 Connect is disabled locally."

That result prints "T3 Connect is disabled locally." and warns that the server's `cloudflared` process may still be running, because a SIGKILLed server can't stop the connector it started and nothing adopts it on restart.

## Scope and approval

A small, focused fix for an obvious bug: one result [...]

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Warn when a stopped server may leave its relay client running.**

When the recorded server PID is dead, the report prints only "T3 Connect is disabled locally." The connector warning appears only after a live unlink fails, so this path drops it. A non-detached `cloudflared` child can outlive a `SIGKILL`ed server. An attached connector keeps its tunnel routing to the persisted local port. The relay step warns only about the relay record.

Do not present rerunning `t3 connect unlink` as the connector cleanup. Relay deletion is refused while the connector is attached, so a rerun does not stop it.

title: perf(server): the headless browser closes after five idle minutes (517 MiB → 1.6 MiB median)

head: 3aa6f6851972fab97c89c00431e110f7a19019a9
body:
## Problem

The server's shared headless Chromium keeps running after an agent's last tab closes. Agents' isolated tabs and recording encoders all use this one browser. Each tab's context closes with the tab, but the browser process stays up until the server exits. On macOS that idle process tree holds about 517 MiB, on a machine where the user may never open another agent tab.

`ServerBrowserContexts` now closes the shared browser after it has held no context for `idleBrowserMs`. `ServerBrowser` sets this to five minutes.

- Opening a shared context clears the timer. When a context closes, the timer is armed again, as long as no other context is still being created.
- When the timer fires, it checks everything again before closing anything: the browser must still be the cached one, have no contexts, and have nothing being created.

- The timer is `unref`'d and is cleared on dispose.
