title: perf(server): PR cache invalidation no longer waits on other projects' reads (1,163 ms → 0.12 ms median)
author: Yuruzuu
head: 09b7f9ba92a91dcae78e683623de0a96704bd8c3
body:
## Problem

Invalidating one PR's cached reads waits for every PR read in flight, in every project. That includes the invalidation after each turn, before each watch read, and around each PR action. One slow host read in another project held them all for the length of its network call.

## Change

`PullRequestReadCache.invalidate` took all 512 permits of the semaphore that every `get` holds one permit of for its whole lookup. The exclusion exists because a read stores its result under the scope revisions it started with. If an invalidation of one of its scopes landed mid-read, that stale result could be served once the new revision expired.

Now scopes hash to 64 lock stripes:

- A `get` takes one permit on each of its scopes' stripes, in sorted order, inside the existing 512-read cap.
- `invalidate` takes the whole stripe for its scope only, then a separate one-permit lock that serializes revision-file writes.
- The writer never waits on a stripe while holding that lock, so this cannot deadlock.

Same-scope reads are still excluded, so stale in-flight results are still rejected. Unrelated scopes wait only on a 1-in-64 stripe collision.

This is server-only and provider-independent, and every client benefits.

title: perf(server): a slow host no longer delays other watched PRs' wakes (935 ms → 65 ms median)
author: Yuruzuu
head: be7648cb43dd513ad77b216096e498cfea61e8e6
body:
## Problem

When several pull requests are watched, one slow host delays the wake for every other watched PR. Each sweep asks every watched PR's host for a fingerprint, then reads no PR at all until the slowest fingerprint answers. A GitHub Enterprise host taking a second, or a request heading toward its 30 s timeout, holds back healthy github.com PRs by that long.

## Change

`PullRequestWatchReactor.sweep` ran `Effect.forEach(groups, fingerprintOf, { concurrency: "unbounded" })` to completion before starting any `readGroup`.

Now every fingerprint is still requested at once, so GitHub's 25-alias batching is unchanged. Each group's read starts as soon as its own fingerprint arrives. A four-permit semaphore keeps the same limit of four group reads in flight. Rate-limited fingerprints still pause their group, and failed ones still fall back to a full read.

This is server-only, and every client benefits. GitHub is the only provider with fingerprints; other providers return `null` at once and read as before. Independent PRs may now wake in a different order. Targets within one PR still dispatch in order.

title: fix(server): Antigravity installs on Intel Macs
author: aledog007
head: 66627bea9053d80f067e2fb0e94b1b0a8a6a683e
body:
## Problem

On Intel Macs, installing the Antigravity ACP runtime from provider settings sticks at "Checking the downloaded runtime" and then fails with the generic "Could not install Antigravity. Check free disk space…" error. The download, SHA-256 check, and extraction all succeed. The runtime then never answers ACP `initialize`, so validation times out after 90 seconds.

Cause: Google signs the darwin-x64 `agy_acp_server.par` and `localharness_external` (1.4.5) with the hardened runtime (`flags=0x10000(runtime)`) and no entitlements. The runtime is a bundled Python program. On x86_64 its `libffi` needs writable+executable memory for closures. Hardened runtime refuses that, so `libffi` falls back to `dlmmap_locked` → `open_temp_exec_file_dir` and retries temp-file mappings forever. A `sample` of the hung process shows it spinning in `open`/`unlink`/`mmap` under `dlmmap_locked`. Run by hand, it printed nothing in 400 seconds. Apple Silicon is unaffected because `libffi` there doesn't need writable executable memory.

## Fix

On darwin-x64 only, after the SHA-256 check passes and before validation, re-sign both binaries ad hoc with `/usr/bin/codesign --force --sign -`. This keeps the integrity check against Google's pinned hash and drops only the hardened-runtime flag. Re-signing changes file sizes, so the install record now stores the sizes measured after signing. Without that, `completedRelease` would reject the installed files.

## Problem

On iOS, after using the in-app microphone in a thread, the composer shows what you type but the draft never updates: the Send button stays disabled and the box doesn't grow. Leaving the thread and coming back fixes it, as does restarting the app.

title: fix(mobile): iOS 26 scroll edge effect no longer hides composer text
author: wojas
head: 806f23b46ddc1bddbedb8384b4c4a54f2dc392ee
body:
## Problem

On iOS 26, the composer sometimes stops drawing typed text while everything else keeps working: the caret and selection handles are visible, typing and autocorrect suggestions work, and the draft is saved. Switching to another app and back makes the text reappear.

A `UITextView` is a scroll view, and iOS 26 can attach a scroll edge effect to it (the blur/fade UIKit puts on scroll content near bars and glass). When that happens to the composer, the effect's backdrop sits over the whole editor. The drawn text and selection highlight are below it, so they disappear. The caret and handles are above it, so they stay visible. Backgrounding the app tears the effect down, which is why switching apps fixes it.

## Change

On iOS 26, the composer's text view hides all four of its edge effects (`topEdgeEffect` … `rightEdgeEffect`) with their public `isHidden` flag. The composer never scrolls under a bar, so the effect has no job there. This only affects the composer's own text view, not the edge effects of the thread feed or other scroll views.

## Scope and approval

This is an 8-line fix for an obvious bug: typed text becomes invisible. It only touches the iOS composer view, behind `#available(iOS 26.0, *)`. Android, web and desktop are unaffected.

author: wojas
head: d6f0248e140cb6bc5f2a7bbcfa2b81d1d14962a1
body:
## Problem

On iOS, the message composer sometimes stops drawing the text you type. The draft is still there: you can select it, the selection handles land where the words should be, and sending works. But no glyphs, selection highlight or handle stems are drawn. Once it happens it lasts until the app restarts. On an iPhone 16 Pro Max running iOS 26 it happened often in normal use.

The cause is in `T3ComposerEditorView.swift`. The view creates its `UITextView` with the default TextKit 2 engine, but it reads `textView.layoutManager` in three places:
- measuring content size;
- hit-testing taps on context chips;
- building VoiceOver elements.

The first such read makes UIKit swap the live text view to TextKit 1 compatibility mode, a one-way switch. With an empty or single-line draft that happens on the first layout. With a multi-line draft it is put off until a tap or until the draft shrinks to one line, so the swap lands mid-edit, and the text view keeps laying out text without drawing it.

## Change

Create the text view on TextKit 1 from the start with `UITextView(usingTextLayoutManager: false)`, so it never swaps engines while live. The composer already ends up on TextKit 1 after the first `layoutManager` read, and all its sizing, hit-testing and accessibility code is written against TextKit 1, so behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

With Proton Pass it offers the account login ("app.t3.codes" plus an email address), which is the wrong thing to offer for a new password and invites filling a login into the field.

It is a masked, single-line password-type input with no keyboard suggestions, and reports `onChangeText` and `onSubmit` to JS.

`SecretTextInput` is a platform split. iOS keeps the existing React Native `TextInput` with its current props. The Android variant draws the same frame as `AppTextInput` (border, radius, background, 54px minimum height) around the native view and passes theme colors in. `SecretRequestCard` just uses it.

title: fix(azure-devops): a fork's same-named branch no longer hides the branch's own pull request
author: saphid
head: 27f40ca144fcf1a0e1b9a114d24ca2466ef1b136
body:
## Problem

On an Azure DevOps repository, T3 Code can miss the open pull request for the branch you're on. This happens when a fork has a newer pull request from a branch with the same name, for example two `feature` branches. The branch then shows no pull request, and the git action offers to create one that already exists.

With no provider `headBranchProbe` hook, the server asks for one open result per branch selector. `az repos pr list --source-branch ` matches that branch name in every fork: the az CLI builds `GitPullRequestSearchCriteria` from `source_ref_name` only and never sets a source repository, and an `owner:branch` selector becomes the bare branch. So the fork's newer pull request takes the single slot. `matchesBranchHeadContext` rejects it, because it is cross-repository and carries no head owner, and the branch's own pull request is never read.

## Change

Add the same `headBranchProbe` hook GitHub already has: drop `owner:branch` selectors, since the caller already checks owners, and read a full page of 100. This is the same fix as #29751 (Bitbucket) and #29791 (GitLab).

## Scope and approval

Very small, focused fix for an obvious bug, so no prior issue: one 5-line provider hook copied from the existing GitHub hook, plus one test. Overlap search: #29751 and #29791 make the same fix for Bitbucket and GitLab only. Closed #27890 was GitCafe fork identity. No open PR touches Azure DevOps branch lookup.

## Verification

- Red on `main`: `vp test run src/server [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**

**Keep the larger response within the process output limit.**

`AzureDevOpsCli.listPullRequests` returns full JSON, but `VcsProcess` truncates output at 1,000,000 bytes. A branch with enough matching PRs and reviewers can now exceed that limit, even when the previous one-result lookup succeeded. The truncated JSON fails decoding, which blocks the PR lookup and creation workflow. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pingdotgg/t3code/27f40ca144fcf1a0e1b9a114d24ca2466ef1b136/packages/source-control-azure-devops/src/server/AzureDevOpsCli.ts))

Limit the returned fields or handle larger responses safely.

title: fix(server): reverting files removes what a new .gitignore from the turn was hiding
author: saphid
head: e13f1b5054196ae904b1e8c4f1daa131763abfba
body:
## Problem

Reverting files to a checkpoint can leave files behind if the agent created a new `.gitignore` during the turns being undone. For example, the agent scaffolds `web/`, writes `web/.gitignore` with `node_modules/`, `dist/` and `.env`, then runs `npm install`. After "Revert files too", `web/node_modules/…` and `web/.env` are still on disk.

The cause is that restore runs `git clean -fd` once. That pass deletes the new `.gitignore` files, but Git read them during the same scan, so it skipped the files they ignored. Once the `.gitignore` is gone, those files are no longer ignored. They show up as untracked (`?? web/`), and the next turn's checkpoint stages them with `git add -A`, so `node_modules` ends up in checkpoint objects and diffs.

## Change

`restoreCheckpoint` repeats `git clean -fd` while the previous pass removed something (at most four passes). It recreates the workspace before each pass, as the existing single pass does. A restore that cleans nothing still runs one pass. Files that stay ignored under the restored rules are still kept, as before.

If the fourth pass still removed something (a chain of more than four nested `.gitignore` files the turn created), restore runs `git clean -dn`. If that still lists paths, restore fails with the same `git clean` error as other clean failures, instead of reporting success with files left behind.

## Scope and approval

title: fix(opencode): tools stopped mid-run show as interrupted, not failed
author: saphid
head: 9450ae0b5d9ea0793a2d4c6aae323aedaac3b61c
body:
## Problem

With OpenCode 1.x, pressing Stop while a tool is running makes OpenCode rewrite that tool part as `status: "error"`, `error: "Tool execution aborted"`, `metadata.interrupted: true`. OpenCode's own UI treats this as cancelled. T3's v1 OpenCode adapter mapped every tool error to `failed`. So every command, edit, or task subagent that was running when the user stopped the turn showed as failed. Stopped edits also showed "Tool execution aborted" as their diff, because the failed path uses the error output as the diff.

## Change

`toolStatus` in the v1 adapter now returns `interrupted` for these parts. It uses the same check as OpenCode's UI: `metadata.interrupted === true` or the abort message. This matches the v2 adapter, which already maps `session.tool.failed` with `error.type === "aborted"` to `interrupted`, and matches Codex. The task subagent status now takes `status.item` directly. The old ternary collapsed every unlisted status to `running`, so a stopped task would have shown as still running.

## Scope and approval

Very small, focused fix for an obvious bug, so no prior issue: one status mapping in one adapter now matches its v2 sibling and OpenCode's own semantics. Overlap search: the local PR index and four `gh search` queries (opencode aborted/interrupted/stop tool, "Tool execution aborted") found nothing related. The closest are #22938 (cancelled todos) and #21979 (failed background subagents), which touch different code paths.

## Verification

- Red o [...]

threads.body:
** Major** · **Functional Correctness** · **Heavy lift**

**Stopped tools can stay running when `session.error` arrives first.**

On stop, OpenCode can publish `session.error` before it sends the interrupted tool update. `finalizeTurn` clears the active turn, so `handlePartUpdated` drops that later update. Tool items that are still open when the turn finalizes receive no terminal status, so a stopped tool can keep its last reported `running` status.

Add a test that delivers `session.error` before the interrupted tool `message.part.updated` event. Assert that the tool reports `interrupted`. Then choose how the adapter should settle open tool items at finalization, or how it should accept terminal tool updates for a finalized turn. This choice changes adapter state handling, so no patch is proposed here.

_Source: Path instructions_

title: fix(server): a publish whose first push fails still shows the new remote
author: saphid
head: 799d458e9a2ffbfd7f9ebed9698d2245c063eef3
body:
## Problem

Publishing a local repository creates the hosted repository and adds it as a remote (for example `origin`) before the first push. If that push fails, for example because SSH authentication is rejected or the host key isn't trusted, the error correctly says "Created owner/repo and added it as remote "origin", but the push failed… then push again."

The panel never learns about the new remote. The `sourceControl.publishRepository` handler refreshed the repository identity and Git status only when the whole publish succeeded. So the status keeps `hasPrimaryRemote: false`: the Git actions menu still offers **Publish**, which would try to create the same repository again. Project grouping by repository identity also stays stale.

## Change

The handler now runs the identity refresh and the status refresh after the publish finishes, whether it succeeded or failed (`Effect.ensuring` instead of two success-only `Effect.tap`s). Both effects already can't fail: `resolve` has no error channel, and `refreshGitStatus` ignores causes and forks. The success path doesn't change.

This matches #29651 (the same success-only refresh in `gitRunStackedAction`) and #19686 (auto-pull).

## Scope and approval

Very small, focused fix for an obvious bug, so no prior issue: the server's own error message describes a partly applied state (remote added) that the status refresh then ignores. It is one handler, with no contract or client change.

title: fix(server): thread titles no longer fail when the text generation provider can't run
author: medric-z
head: dabdbb5f343fe038639e6e893cf83c4e1ec70d46
body:
## Problem

Codex is the default text generation provider (`gpt-6-luna`), and it is enabled by default. If the Codex CLI is not installed, or is installed but signed out, every thread title, branch name, and commit message request still goes to Codex and fails. Titles silently stay as the truncated first message. This hits anyone on default settings who uses a different provider, such as Claude-only setups (#26962).

Both states are already detected by the provider probe:

- **Not installed:** `installed: false`, `status: "error"`.
- **Signed out:** `installed: true`, `status: "error"`, `auth.status: "unauthenticated"`. Codex retries five times and fails with `401 Unauthorized` after about 16 s.

## Change

`TextGeneration.generate` already switches to the fallback provider when the selected model's usage window is exhausted. A selected provider whose probe failed because it is missing or signed out now takes the same path:

```ts
const unusable =
  selected?.enabled === true &&
  selected.status === "error" &&
  (!selected.installed || selected.auth.status === "unauthenticated");
if (unusable || exhaustedUsageWindow(selected, now, selection.model)) {
```

- A pending probe (`status: "warning"`) keeps its selection, so nothing switches while providers are still being checked at startup.
- The fallback candidate filter already skips missing and signed-out providers, so this applies the same rule to the selected one.
- The condition is not Codex-specific.

author: Jerematix
head: 44ea3d5fcb24c62aa627e33565601cdc35c85cf3
body:
## Problem

On iPhone with the floating glass tab bar (iOS 26+), the compose button next to the tabs can grow to about 1.16× (62pt → ~72pt) when you switch tabs, for example Settings → Chats. It stays enlarged until the bar happens to lay out again, which can take a second or more.

## Change

`WorkspaceTabBar.layoutSubviews` sizes compose from the union of the tab buttons. When the `workspace-tab-*` identifiers aren't found, it falls back to every visible control in the bar. The fix measures only controls whose converted size equals their own bounds, so anything drawn under a scaling transform is skipped. If nothing qualifies, compose keeps its last frame, as it already does when the row is empty.

title: fix(gitlab): the checks panel lists each pipeline job
author: TonybynMp4
head: d28b2e8ef11235e1bcefc74eae7fbf818db58167
body:
## Problem

A GitLab merge request shows its whole head pipeline as one "Pipeline" check. When it fails, the checks panel can't say which job broke, so you have to open GitLab to find out. GitHub pull requests list each check in the same panel. Fixes #13431.

## Change

The checks and detail reads now also ask GitLab's GraphQL API for the head pipeline's stages and their jobs, in one request alongside the existing trigger job read.

- Each job becomes a check named after its stage, like `test / unit`, with GitLab's status and label, linking to the job log.
- Jobs allowed to fail show as neutral. Retried attempts are left out, so a job counts by its latest run. Manual jobs stay neutral.
- A stage whose job list GitLab didn't return whole stays one check with GitLab's stage status. That covers more than 100 jobs, jobs GitLab couldn't resolve, and jobs without a name.
- If the stages can't be read whole, or the pipeline has none, the single "Pipeline" check stays as before.
- Trigger job rows from #24688 are still appended after the jobs.

The read sits behind the existing `downstreamChecks` flag, so the permission check before writes still skips it. No paging, no cache, no new setting. Everything is in `packages/source-control-gitlab`.

## Scope and approval

#13431 is a triaged bug (`accepted`). An earlier attempt, #13434, listed every job over REST and was closed as too large. GraphQL removes the paging, caching and trigger status logic that made it big.

This PR first showed [...]

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Handle a truncated `stages` connection before replacing the pipeline check.**

GitLab permits user-defined stages and does not document a 100-stage limit. If a failed stage is after the first 100 stages, `getMergeRequestDetail` can receive only successful earlier stages and replace the failed `Pipeline` check with them. Add `pageInfo.hasNextPage` handling for `stages`, and retain the pipeline fallback or paginate when the stage connection is truncated.

Job truncation has a narrower effect. If failed jobs are beyond `jobs(first: 100)`, the decoder still emits the stage with `status: "failure"`. Only the individual failed-job checks and log links are incomplete.

✅ Addressed in commit 3d4e04f

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Return `null` when the GraphQL response carries `errors` or a `null` stage node. Otherwise a failed stage can be dropped.**

`decodePipelineStageChecksJson` uses `data` without checking top-level `errors`. `RawPipelineStagesSchema` has no `errors` field.

GraphQL can return partial data. A stage that GitLab fails to resolve then appears as a `null` node next to an `errors` entry. The loop at Line 390 skips `null` stages and stages without a name. The caller replaces the single "Pipeline" check with the remaining stages. If the dropped stage is the failed one, the checks panel shows only passing stages. This is the false-green result that the `null` fallback exists to prevent. The existing test covers only an error response with no `data`.

Treat any `errors` entry, and any `null` stage node, as unreadable. Then the caller keeps the single pipeline check.

Based on learnings: when a GraphQL response must succeed completely, check top-level `errors` before consuming `data`. No client or other layer here handles partial data. `graphqlRead` passes the raw body straight to this decoder.

_Source: Learnings_

✅ Addressed in commi [...]

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Treat a stage with no name as incomplete data, not as a skipped stage.**

`decodePipelineStageChecksJson` drops a stage with a null name. The `if (stage === null || name === null) continue;` check skips it without returning `null`. If that stage failed, the checks panel omits the failure. When other stages have names, the function returns a non-empty list, so the `Pipeline` fallback is not kept. The function's own comment says a missing stage "could be the failed one," and it applies that rule to null stage nodes but not to nameless stages.

✅ Addressed in commit 0048ed6

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win**

**Keep the failed stage when a job node or name is missing.**

GitLab GraphQL connections allow nullable nodes. A failed stage can therefore contain one named failed job and one null job node without a top-level GraphQL error. The decoder drops the incomplete job and replaces the stage with only the named job, so the failed-job display is incomplete.

title: fix(mobile): Android app no longer stays offline after reopening
author: kahlstrm
head: 78aa37c3b3f3a920a550ef5d71cefdf4935509be
body:
## Problem

On Android 15+, reopening the app sometimes leaves it on "You are offline" with no connection attempts, until it is backgrounded and reopened again. Fixes https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/28624.

Android blocks a backgrounded app's network and lifts the block shortly after the app returns to the foreground. If the app reads its network state before the block lifts, expo-network reports offline. Android reports the lift only through `NetworkCallback.onBlockedStatusChanged`, which expo-network doesn't implement, so the connection supervisor never sees an online report and never retries.

## Change

Add `onBlockedStatusChanged` to the existing expo-network patch. It re-reads the network state and emits it, like the other network callbacks. `expo-network` is already in `buildFromSource`, so the patch takes effect. `pnpm-lock.yaml` changes only the patch hash. The upstream report is https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/52725; this hunk can be dropped once Expo ships a fix.

## Scope and approval

A very small, focused fix for an obvious bug: five lines in an existing dependency patch, with no change to T3 code, settings or product behaviour. The app already reconnects on an online report; this makes expo-network deliver one when Android lifts the block.

## Verification

Release APKs built at `da21606` with and without this change, on an Android 16 emulator, using an automated lab: https://github.com/kahlstrm/config/tree/main/infra/experiments/t3-mobile

- **Shell, thread, and config streams waited for an ack after every chunk.** The server now keeps up to 8 chunks in flight for them, the same window terminal output uses. - **Reopening after a long background waited too long to replace a dead socket.** The silent-socket check skips the 2.5 s wait meant for live remote sockets and gives up after 1.5 s. A socket that delivers a frame during the check gets 3 s, counted from the resume.

## Problem

On iOS, if an autocorrection is pending when you tap Send (for example "teh" → "the"), the message goes out with the uncorrected word and the composer then fills back up with the whole draft, now containing the corrected word. You have to clear the composer by hand.

title: fix(web): PR bodies keep before/after video tables intact
author: bartlomiejbloniarz
head: 37d33d6b8e9cca683f434cbc1dabc690c9f80822
body:
## Problem

A PR description that shows media side by side in an HTML table renders broken in the PR panel. This is GitHub's usual layout for before/after recordings. The videos are lifted out of their cells and stacked at full width, and the header row is left on its own. This happens on web, desktop and mobile.

The PR body splitter lifts any line that is only a video link out of the Markdown, so the video can play inline. It did not know when that line was inside a ``, so it cut tables apart.

## Change

The splitter in `client-runtime` now recognises an HTML `` with an attachment link in its cells. It returns the table as one segment, and each cell is split on its own. Web and mobile render that segment as rows of equal-width columns. The mobile description preview also collects attachments from inside tables.

Any other table goes through the line-by-line splitter as before. This covers tables without attachment links (including Markdown image-only tables), tables with content outside their cells such as a caption, nested tables and unclosed tables.

## Follow-up PRs

This is the first of four PRs about media in PR descriptions. The other three build on it and fix how videos look on mobile and web. They come from a fork, so they can't use this PR's branch as their base. I'll open each one after the PR below it merges, so its diff contains only its own change:

title: fix(mobile): keyboard state follows Android's nonanimated IME show
author: juliusmarminge
head: 4251a0cc71c14ad2eeefa1f66a4ef5f814dab499
body:
## Problem

On Android, when the IME inset changes without an animation (for example on split-screen or resume), `react-native-keyboard-controller`'s desync repair (`syncKeyboardPosition`) emits `keyboardDidShow` with no `keyboardWillShow` first. The library's imperative cache (`KeyboardController.isVisible()`/`state()`) and `useKeyboardState` only listen to `keyboardWillShow`, so they stay hidden at height 0 while the keyboard is on screen, and `KeyboardController.dismiss()` resolves immediately instead of waiting for the native hide. Reproduced on current `main` by emitting `keyboardDidHide(0)` then `keyboardDidShow(376)` into the real library module and a mounted hook: both report hidden/0, and dismissal settles before `keyboardDidHide`.

## Change

Extend the existing `react-native-keyboard-controller@1.22.8` patch so the module cache handles `keyboardDidShow` the same way it handles `keyboardWillShow`, and `useKeyboardState` subscribes to `keyboardDidShow` too. `keyboardWillShow` handling stays, so the hook still updates as soon as the keyboard starts showing. The change is applied to `src`, `lib/commonjs` and `lib/module`; the lockfile patch hash is updated. A stale comment in `ThreadTerminalRouteScreen.tsx` that described the old event set is corrected.

The approach follows the reporter's fix in https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/22514 (and the same dependency change proposed in https://git.cafe/pingdotgg/t3code/pulls/21595), rebuilt on the 1.22.8 patch that repl [...]

title: fix(mobile): Android terminal Backspace deletes on the first press
author: only21mil
head: 29d53bdbce56f96e501bff158273442a992f1dc0
body:
## Problem

On Android, Backspace in the integrated terminal can do nothing with some keyboards. With FUTO Keyboard the first presses are swallowed and deletion only starts after several more. The reporter says Samsung Keyboard works and that FUTO works in Termux on the same phone (#8253).

The terminal's hidden input field clears after every change, because typed text goes straight to the shell. A keyboard that sends `KEYCODE_DEL` reaches the key listener and works. A keyboard that deletes through `InputConnection.deleteSurroundingText` (or `deleteSurroundingTextInCodePoints`) asks the empty field to delete text it no longer has, so nothing reaches the shell. FUTO, like the AOSP keyboard it is based on, uses that call while its own record of the field still holds the characters it typed. On main in an Android 16 emulator, after typing 11 characters with FUTO, the first 11 Backspace presses deleted nothing and the 12th deleted one character.

title: fix(desktop): quit no longer orphans a backend that is slow to stop
author: saphid
head: f4877a8bbf39507b8f53c73f0b841cb971925376
body:
## Problem

Quitting the desktop app can leave its backend child running as an orphan. When a backend's graceful shutdown takes longer than the 5 second SIGTERM grace, the app exits anyway. The backend keeps running under launchd (ppid 1), still holding `statev2.sqlite` and its provider agents, until the next launch cleans it up. On a real install this made quit look hung for over 10 minutes, and an offline database repair could not get the database to itself.

The cause is a timeout race. `stopAllPoolInstances` waits `stop({ timeout: 5s })` per backend. Closing the run scope reaches the spawner's release (`terminateProcessGroup`): SIGTERM to the process group, wait `forceKillAfter` (`DEFAULT_BACKEND_TERMINATE_GRACE`, 5 s), then SIGKILL and up to one more second for the group to exit. The quit wait equals the grace, so it expires first, `markComplete` lets the app exit, and the pending SIGKILL dies with the process. The updater does the same before `quitAndInstall`.

## Change

`DesktopBackendManager` exports `BACKEND_QUIT_STOP_TIMEOUT`, the grace plus 2 seconds to cover the SIGKILL and the spawner's one-second exit wait. Quit (`stopAllPoolInstances`) and the updater's pre-install stop both use it. The grace is unchanged at 5 s. A backend whose teardown truly never finishes still cannot hold quit past the bound; the existing test for that now uses the new bound.

## Scope and approval

A very small, focused fix for an obvious bug: two call sites used a deadline equal to the k [...]

** Major** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Quick win**

**Cover the deadline selected by the desktop quit path.**

The new test supplies `BACKEND_QUIT_STOP_TIMEOUT` directly to `instance.stop`. It does not exercise the `DesktopApp` quit helper. The existing shutdown test also has an empty backend pool, so a regression to the five-second caller timeout would still pass both tests.

Extend the existing `DesktopApp.test.ts` shutdown case with a delayed backend. Assert that `DesktopApp.program` remains pending after five seconds and completes after the delayed backend exits.

- The platform is Windows.
- The executable is Git for Windows' real binary, `\\bin\git.exe`, not the `cmd\git.exe` launcher or a Scoop shim. Those allocate a console for their child.
- The args exactly match one of 11 read forms the status refresh issues, optionally after one `--git-dir `. title: fix(server): a command id reused for two threads at once no longer succeeds for both
author: saphid
head: e12d2c979647adc288c1541582642fe380af44f7
body:
## Problem

When two commands with the same `commandId` target different threads at the same time, both report success, but only one thread changes. Each command checks for an existing receipt before planning, under its own thread's lock, so both see none. One commits first. The other's `insertIfAbsent` loses and hands back the winner's receipt, and the dispatcher returned it as the loser's own successful result, because after commit it only checked for a rejected receipt.

## Change

After `eventSink.commitCommand`, `dispatchWithReceiptEffect` now checks the committed receipt with the existing `canReplayCommandReceipt` helper before any post-commit work (queue resume, notification delivery) and before reporting success. A receipt for another thread fails the command with `OrchestratorCommandIdConflictError`, the same error the pre-planning receipt check already raises and that `ThreadMessageIntake` already maps. The zero-event no-op path and the rejection path are unchanged: neither can report another thread's success.

## Scope and approval

Small, focused fix for an obvious correctness bug (a command reports a success that did not happen), so it uses the no-prior-issue exception. Ten lines in the dispatcher plus a regression test.

## Verification

- New test `Orchestrator.receipt-race.test.ts` uses the real orchestrator, event sink, receipt store, and in-memory SQLite. A `Deferred` gate in the fake adapter's capability lookup holds both `thread.model-selection.set` comman [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win**

**Check thread ownership before replaying rejection details.**

When the zero-event path loses `insertIfAbsent`, `replayCommandReceipt` returns the stored `receipt.error` before checking `receipt.threadId`. A rejected receipt from another thread can therefore expose that thread's rejection detail through the websocket response and return `OrchestratorCommandPreviouslyRejectedError` instead of `OrchestratorCommandIdConflictError`. Check thread ownership first. Preserve rejection details only for same-thread replays.

title: fix(server): coalesce tool output before it fills the live buffer
author: snarkyalyx
head: 683a0ed60209494f49747ab18f113fcca437ade1
body:
Bursts of full updates for a running tool can fill the live-event buffer before the 50 ms batching window expires. The server retains superseded updates and checks the limit before deduplicating them. On the original code, 150 updates with 64 KiB of output each reproduce `LiveStreamBufferError` at the default 8 MiB limit.

This change replaces pending updates for the same thread, run, and tool as they arrive, releasing the superseded buffer charge immediately. Updates remain in sequence order, completion and other lifecycle events flush the window, and queued or unacknowledged events remain charged. Both buffer limits stay unchanged.

This is a focused fix for an existing deduplication path applying its reduction too late, rather than a new streaming policy or configurable limit.

Validation:

- All 94 focused tests pass across the coalescer, buffer, client thread/shell synchronization, and RPC subscriptions.
- The byte-limit, item-limit, and default 8 MiB regression tests fail on the original code and pass with this change.
- Recovery tests verify that undelivered events replay without gaps or duplicates after overflow. Oversized replacements still fail and clean up; slow-subscriber and unacknowledged-delivery tests also pass.
- Server typecheck, targeted lint and formatting checks, and server bundle build pass.

The reported session freezes prompted this investigation, but the logs do not identify the overflowing subscription. This fix addresses a reproduced overflow trigge [...]

threads.body:
** Minor** · **Performance & Scalability** · **Quick win**

**Avoid rebuilding the full pending batch for each event.**

`coalesceThreadLiveStream` passes each source batch to `offerAll`, which holds the mutex while `LiveStreamBudget.replace` maps, reduces, and scans the retained batch for every event. The 50 ms timer cannot interrupt that critical section because it also waits for the mutex. This can keep the event loop and subscriber mutex busy for materially longer than the prior path, which retained each event and performed the full replacement only at flush.

Refactor the coalescer and budget update so each event changes only the affected retained items while preserving byte and item accounting. The `WeakMap` prevents repeated `JSON.stringify`, but it does not prevent the repeated batch allocations and scans.

✅ Addressed in commit 61b561a
